label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 3 pilot (live recorded window), not the evaluation

report.summary: Outbox delivery stalled for about 90 s because the external consumer refused connections. Transfers kept committing, so a backlog built and notifications were delayed, then drained in a burst.

findings.claim: Transfer intake was healthy: 468 requests, all 201, p95 0.24 s. The delay is not in the API path.
findings.reason: No server errors and normal latency on /v1/transfers.

findings.claim: Publications dropped to 0 for about 90 s while arrivals continued at 32 per 10 s. Pending grew to 287 and oldest age reached 116 s.
findings.reason: Per-bucket counts show the publication gap, and the pending and age gauges rose in step; publications resumed at 80 per bucket.

findings.claim: The stall coincided with 1532 CONNECTION_FAILED attempts (~0.3 ms each) from the outbox to the consumer. There were no auth or server errors.
findings.reason: All failures are network errors that fail instantly with no consumer record. Successful attempts took ~72 ms and the consumer handler ~0.02 ms.

limitations: The reason the consumer refused connections (down, restarting, network) is not visible from these tools.
Only the earliest log rows are listed, so the exact start and end of the failure period come from the bucket counts.
next_checks: Check the external consumer's availability, restarts and listener logs around 09:43:33 to 09:44:50.
Review the outbox retry/backoff settings, since attempts failed every ~1 s and the drain was a burst.

alternatives.reason: Successful deliveries were fast (p95 74 ms; handler 0.03 ms), and the failures were instant connection refusals.
alternatives.hypothesis: Slow consumer processing or auth caused the delay

alternatives.reason: Requests were all 201 with low latency, and arrivals were steady.
alternatives.hypothesis: Transfer API slowness or errors delayed event creation

report.summary: Transfers are accepted fast, but outbox publication stalled for about 90 s because delivery attempts failed with connection errors. The backlog and undelivered age grew, which fits late notifications.

findings.claim: The transfer API is healthy; the delay is downstream of the request path.
findings.reason: All 468 requests returned 201, p99 was 0.248 s and the server error ratio was 0.

findings.claim: Outbox publication stopped for about 90 s while arrivals continued, building a backlog; the oldest undelivered age reached 116 s.
findings.reason: Publications were 0 in buckets 4-12 and 80 per bucket later, while arrivals stayed at 32. Pending peaked at 287.

findings.claim: The stall coincides with connection failures to the delivery endpoint: 1532 of 1867 attempts were CONNECTION_FAILED.
findings.reason: Failed attempts had no consumer record and took about 0.3 ms, which fits refused connections. Successful attempts took about 72 ms with status 200.

findings.claim: The consumer was unreachable or refusing connections for part of the window. This was likely the cause, and publication recovered with catch-up bursts.
findings.reason: Failures were network-level, with no server or auth errors, and success resumed at 80 per bucket. The tools do not show why the connections failed.

alternatives.hypothesis: Slow or erroring consumer processing caused the delay.
alternatives.reason: Successful attempts were fast (about 72 ms) and there were no server or auth errors.

alternatives.hypothesis: A LedgerCore-side outbox poller or network problem, not the consumer, caused the connection failures.
alternatives.reason: The failures are client-side connection errors, and the evidence cannot tell which side caused them.

limitations: Only the earliest 100 of 1867 delivery log rows are listed, so the exact end of the failure period comes from the bucket counts rather than from logs.
No data on the consumer's availability or on network or DNS state, so the root cause of the connection failures is unknown.
next_checks: Check consumer endpoint availability, restarts and listener state from about 09:43:30 to 09:44:55.
Review the outbox retry/backoff configuration and any network or DNS changes in that period.
